bash -c '
# --- Mini Shai-Hulud IOC Scanner ---
# This hook runs AFTER every bash command Claude Code executes.
# It checks if an npm/pip install just happened, and if so, scans for known
# indicators of compromise (IOCs) from the Shai-Hulud worm.

# Only trigger after install commands
TOOL_INPUT="$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT"
if echo "$TOOL_INPUT" | grep -qiE "npm install|npm i |npm ci|pip install|yarn add|pnpm add|bun add"; then

  FOUND=0

  # Check 1: Suspicious files in config directories
  for f in .claude/setup.mjs .claude/router_runtime.js .vscode/setup.mjs; do
    if [ -f "$f" ]; then
      echo "[ALERT] Suspicious file found: $f — possible Shai-Hulud persistence hook"
      FOUND=1
    fi
  done

  # Check 2: Known malicious filenames in node_modules
  if [ -d "node_modules" ]; then
    HITS=$(find node_modules -maxdepth 3 \( -name "router_init.js" -o -name "tanstack_runner.js" -o -name "router_runtime.js" \) 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$HITS" ]; then
      echo "[ALERT] Known IOC files in node_modules:"
      echo "$HITS"
      FOUND=1
    fi
  fi

  # Check 3: Suspicious domains in recently installed packages
  if [ -d "node_modules" ]; then
    DOMAIN_HITS=$(grep -rl "getsession\.org\|git-tanstack\.com\|cloud-aws\.adc-e\.uk" node_modules/ --include="*.js" --include="*.json" 2>/dev/null | head -10)
    if [ -n "$DOMAIN_HITS" ]; then
      echo "[ALERT] Suspicious C2 domains found in:"
      echo "$DOMAIN_HITS"
      FOUND=1
    fi
  fi

  # Check 4: Git commit hash IOC in package.json files
  if grep -r "79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c" package.json node_modules/*/package.json 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[ALERT] Known malicious git commit hash found in dependencies"
    FOUND=1
  fi

  if [ "$FOUND" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "[OK] Post-install IOC scan clean"
  else
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "  SUPPLY CHAIN COMPROMISE DETECTED"  
    echo "  Do NOT proceed. Alert Niranjan."  
    echo "========================================"
  fi
fi
'

bash -c '
# --- Pre-install safety check ---
# Warns before running npm install (as opposed to npm ci)
# in what looks like a CI/production context.

TOOL_INPUT="$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT"

# Flag if using `npm install` instead of `npm ci` when a lockfile exists
if echo "$TOOL_INPUT" | grep -qE "npm install" && [ -f "package-lock.json" ]; then
  if echo "$TOOL_INPUT" | grep -qvE "--ignore-scripts"; then
    echo "[WARNING] Using npm install instead of npm ci, and --ignore-scripts is not set."
    echo "Lockfile exists — consider: npm ci --ignore-scripts"
    echo "This is safer against supply chain attacks (Shai-Hulud worm uses preinstall hooks)."
  fi
fi
'
